CT HEAD WITHOUT CONTRAST

Indication: Severe headache, dizziness.
Comparison: None.

Findings: No intracranial hemorrhage, mass, mass effect or midline shift. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Ventricles and sulci normal in size for age. Basal cisterns patent. No extra-axial collection. Calvarium intact. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells clear.
reports.conclusion: Normal noncontrast CT of the head.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED PROVIDER NOTE

Chief complaint: headache x2 days, dizzy

HPI: 36M, schizophrenia and diabetes, prior pheochromocytoma (left adrenal, resected), and an oculogyric crisis six months ago. Two days of severe, throbbing headache across the front of his head with dizziness that comes and goes. Bright light and loud noise make it worse. On arrival he is visibly frustrated and pacing the triage area.

PMH: HTN, DM2, schizophrenia, CKD, obesity; s/p L adrenalectomy 2022.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril; also listed risperidone 3 mg BID, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, atenolol 50.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, social EtOH, warehouse associate.
FHx: maternal uncle schizophrenia; father DM2; mother HTN.

Exam: BP 158/94, HR 102, afebrile. No focal neurologic deficits. Fundi normal bilaterally. Neck supple. Became increasingly agitated when told about the wait for CT - raised his voice, fists clenched - and settled with reassurance and a quiet room.

Labs: glucose 180, HbA1c 8.2%, Na 140, K 4.1, creatinine 1.0.
CT head without contrast: normal.

ED course: ketorolac 15 mg IV, normal saline 1 L IV, acetaminophen 1 g PO. Avoided prochlorperazine/metoclopramide given recent dystonic reaction. Headache improved to mild by 15:30, dizziness resolved, tolerating PO.

Impression: Migraine without aura.

Plan: discharge. Naproxen 500 mg BID PRN up to 5 days. Rest, dark room, hydration. PCP follow-up this week. Return for worst headache of life, weakness, numbness, vision loss, fever, stiff neck.

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u ED 4/10 - migraine without aura, normal head CT.

Headache gone since Friday. Used naproxen twice. Light/noise sensitivity resolved. Apologetic about getting upset in the ER, said the waiting and the pain got to him. Mood otherwise his baseline; risperidone 3 BID with psych.

BP 138/86. Neuro: alert, CN intact, strength and gait normal. Fundi not examined today.

ED labs: A1c 8.2, glucose 180, creatinine 1.0, K 4.1.

A/P
1. Migraine without aura: this episode resolved. Naproxen with food only for a bad one, short term. Headache diary; call if they recur. Pheo surveillance in January was normal.
2. DM2: A1c 8.2, up from 7.8. Continue metformin 1000 BID, reviewed diet again; recheck July.
3. HTN: 138/86 today, continue.
RTC July.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted last night, seen first thing.

Two days of burning when he urinates and going much more often. No fever or chills, no back or flank pain, no blood he has noticed, no discharge. Never had this before.

Vitals as charted, afebrile.
Abdomen soft, no suprapubic or CVA tenderness.

Urine dip in office: leukocyte esterase positive, nitrite positive. Culture sent.

A/P
UTI in a man, uncomplicated clinically. Ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID x7 days. Phenazopyridine 200 mg TID for 2 days for the burning - warned it turns urine orange. Fluids. Will call with culture. Call if fever, flank pain or not better in 48 hours.

events.reason: Shortness of breath, blue lips and fingers

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY MEDICINE NOTE

CC: short of breath, lips and fingers blue

HPI: 36-year-old man with schizophrenia and CKD, previously seen in this ED for an oculogyric crisis and for migraine. Two hours ago, after taking the medicines his PCP prescribed this morning for a new urinary tract infection (ciprofloxacin and phenazopyridine), he became suddenly short of breath and noticed his lips and fingertips turning blue. He felt fine before taking them.

PMH: schizophrenia, DM2, HTN, CKD, obesity, s/p left adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma, migraine.
Meds: risperidone 3 mg BID, metformin 1000 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, HCTZ 25 mg, atenolol 50 mg; ciprofloxacin and phenazopyridine started today.
Allergies: NKDA on file.
Social hx: never smoker, social alcohol, warehouse associate.

Exam: RR 28, SpO2 85% on room air and unchanged on 100% oxygen by non-rebreather. Anxious. Central and peripheral cyanosis. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

ABG on 100% O2: PaO2 98 mmHg, PaCO2 38 mmHg, methemoglobin 15%. CBC, electrolytes and renal function within normal limits.

Assessment: acquired methemoglobinemia, symptomatic, from phenazopyridine.

ED course: phenazopyridine discontinued. Methylene blue 1 mg/kg IV over 5 minutes at 14:20. Repeat co-oximetry at 15:15: methemoglobin 2.1%. SpO2 97% on room air by 15:20, cyanosis cleared, breathing comfortably. Observed until evening without recurrence.

Disposition: home. Do NOT take phenazopyridine again - added to allergy list here; please update primary care record. Continue ciprofloxacin as prescribed. PCP follow-up in 2-3 days. Return for any recurrence of blue color or breathlessness.

documents.title: Urine culture result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Jorge. Urine culture grew E. coli, sensitive to ciprofloxacin, so the antibiotic is the right one - finish all 7 days. Urinary symptoms already better. He's shaken up about Monday. Read the ED note: methemoglobinemia from the phenazopyridine, treated with methylene blue. Coming in tomorrow.

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after the ED on Monday.

Within a couple of hours of the first doses of cipro and phenazopyridine I prescribed Monday morning he became short of breath and blue; ED found methemoglobin 15%, gave methylene blue, level 2.1% an hour later, home that night. Since then completely fine. No breathlessness, color normal. Burning gone. On day 4 of cipro.

Vitals as charted; SpO2 normal on room air.
Lips and nail beds pink. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No CVA tenderness.

A/P
1. Methemoglobinemia from phenazopyridine - resolved. Phenazopyridine entered as an allergy (methemoglobinemia, severe). Told him to tell any pharmacy or ER, and to avoid the OTC urinary pain tablets with the same ingredient.
2. UTI, E. coli, cipro-sensitive - improving; finish cipro.
3. Flu shot today.
RTC December for diabetes.
